bills.title: Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons (Amendment) Act 2026
bills.presenter: Datuk Seri Dr. Shamsul Anuar bin Haji Nasarah (Timbalan Menteri Dalam Negeri)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons Act 1969 (“Act 7”) to provide for registrable particulars of a person convicted of registrable offence becoming spent. 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and the provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 7 to introduce the definition of “crime-free period” for the purposes of the new provisions relating to registrable particulars becoming spent. 4. Clause 3 seeks to introduce new sections 13a, 13b and 13c into Act 7. The proposed new section 13a seeks to provide for registrable particulars becoming spent, including the eligibility requirement, applicable crime-free period and circumstances under which the registrable particulars cease to be eligible to become spent. The proposed new section 13b seeks to provide for the effect of registrable particulars of a person convicted of a registrable offence becoming spent. Upon the registrable particulars becoming spent, the registrable particulars shall be treated as no longer registered in the register and as if the person has not been convicted of the registrable offence to which the spent registrable particulars relate. The new section 13b further provides even though the registrable particulars has become spent, the registrable particulars shall remain recorded in the register for the purposes of record by the Registrar. The proposed new section 13c seeks to provide that the registrable particulars of a person which has become spent shall be revived if during or after the expiry of a crime-free period, the person is convicted of any registrable offence specified in the First Schedule. The proposed new section also seeks to provide that if the registrable particulars of the person is revived, the registrable particulars of the person shall be treated as if they have never become spent under Act 7. 5. Clause 4 seeks to amend subsection 15(1) of Act 7 to empower the Minister to amend the proposed new Fourth Schedule. 6. Clause 5 seeks to introduce a new Fourth Schedule into Act 7 to provide the list of registrable offences for which registrable particulars are not eligible to become spent. 7. Clause 6 deals with saving provision.

bills.title: Adoption (Amendment) Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Datuk Seri Dr. Shamsul Anuar bin Haji Nasarah (Timbalan Menteri Dalam Negeri)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Adoption Act 1952 (“Act 257”). 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and the provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 257 in the definition of “child” to lower the age of child from twenty-one years to eighteen years so as to be consistent with the age limit to apply for citizenship by registration as provided in the Constitution (Amendment) Act 2025 [Act A1752], the age for voting in Malaysia as provided in the Federal Constitution, the definition of child as provided in the Child Act 2001 [Act 611] and the age of majority as provided in the Age of Majority Act 1971 [Act 21]. 4. Clause 3 deals with saving provision.

bills.title: Sport Development (Amendment) Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Dr. Mohammed Taufiq Johari (Menteri Belia dan Sukan)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Sports Development Act 1997 (“Act 576”), among others, to introduce a new part relating to enforcement and investigation, to provide for the management and disposal of asset, and liabilities of a sports body the registration of which has been revoked to protect the creditor’s interest and stakeholder, and to provide for the institution of prosecution. This proposed amendment also to empower the Minister to make regulations in respect of compliance with international obligations in relation to anti-doping and any matter relating to safe sport. 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 576 by inserting the new definition of “Court” means the High Court. 4. Clause 3 seeks to substitute subsection 3(2) of Act 576 to provide that the Minister may issue guidelines consistent with international guidelines or rules. 5. Clauses 4, 5 and 6 seek to amend subsections 8(2), 9a(2) and 9b(2) of Act 576 to substitute the term “athletics competitions” with “sporting events” to ensure uniformity and accuracy in the usage of terminology and to avoid confusion with the sport of athletics specified in the First Schedule to the Act 576. 6. Clause 7 seeks to introduce new sections 19a, 19b and 19c into Act 576. The proposed new section 19a seeks to provide for matters relating to the movable and immovable property of a sports body, legal capacity of a sports body to sue and be sued, judgment and execution of judgment against a sports body, criminal liability of a member of a sports body and the dissolution of a sports body. The proposed new section 19b seeks to empower the Commissioner to issue a written direction to a sports body requiring the sports body to amend its constitution or rules within the time specified in the direction after taking into consideration the representation made by the sports body. The proposed new section 19c seeks to provide that a sports body shall not change its name, place of business, registered address or correspondence address or amend its constitution or rules without prior approval of the Commissioner. This clause also provides for the non-compliance with this new proposed section as an offence. 7. Clause 8 seeks to introduce new sections 25a, 25b and 25c into Act 576. The proposed new section 25a seeks to provide for the consequences of the revocation of registration of a sports body by the Commissioner or by virtue of the order made by the Minister under section 41a, including the vesting of property in the Director General of Insolvency for the purpose of winding up the affairs of the sports body. This clause also empowers the Commissioner and Director General of Insolvency to require any information relating to the property, affairs, business, accounts or books of the sports body, or any other matters relating to the sports body. This clause also provides for the non-compliance with subsection 25a(2) as an offence. The proposed new section 25b seeks to provide for the procedure for the vesting of the assets, debts and liabilities of a sports body the registration of which has been revoked in a new registered sports body, subject to an application by the new sports body to the Director General of Insolvency who will then apply for an order from the High Court. The proposed new section 25c seeks to provide for the inspection of any document filed with the Commissioner and enable any person to obtain any copy of the document upon receipt of the prescribed fee subject to the conditions specified in subsection 25c(2). 8. Clause 9 seeks to introduce a new Part VIa into Act 576 which consists of new sections 32a, 32b, 32c, 32d, 32e, 32f, 32g and 32h. The proposed new section 32a seeks to provide for the appointment of enforcement officers by the Minister. The proposed new section 32b seeks to empower an enforcement officer or police officer to carry out any investigation and enforcement of any provision under Act 576. The proposed new section 32c seeks to provide that an enforcement officer shall declare his office and produce his authority card when exercising his powers under Act 576. The proposed new section 32d seeks to provide for the power of enforcement officer or police officer to examine any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of a case and to record any statement made. This clause also provides that any statement made by the person examined shall be admissible as evidence under Act 576 in any proceedings in court. The proposed new section 32e seeks to provide for the power of enforcement officer or police officer to require any person to submit to him any book, minute book, register, financial statement, document, any particular or other things whether in physical or electronic form, and the enforcement officer or police officer may inspect, make copies of, take extracts from, remove and detain any book, minute book, register, financial statement, document, particular or other things whether in physical or electronic form. The proposed new section 32f seeks to provide for the seizure of any book, minute book, register, etc., if the enforcement officer or police officer has reason to believe that an offence has been committed under Act 576. This clause also provides that any book, minute book, register, etc., seized shall be admissible as evidence in any proceedings in court. bills.title: National Trust Fund Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Tuan Liew Chin Tong, Timbalan Menteri Kewangan
bills.explanation: The National Trust Fund Bill 2026 (“the proposed Act”) seeks to repeal the National Trust Fund Act 1988 [Act 339] (“the repealed Act”) and reestablish the National Trust Fund (“the Fund”). Under the proposed Act, the Fund will continue to be maintained and replenished since the utilisation of RM5 billion from the Fund for the purchase of Covid-19 vaccines in 2021. The proposed Act also seeks to incorporate the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) as the governing body of the Fund and provide for the investment of the Fund. The proposed Act aims to ensure the continued growth of the Fund. Strict conditions and procedures are imposed for the utilisation of the Fund as the Fund is intended to serve as a long-lasting financial reserve for the benefit of current and future generations of Malaysia. The proposed Act also seeks to introduce reform of the Fund in three main aspects: (a) placing contributions to the Fund on a broad and mandatory statutory footing, beyond voluntary payments; (b) preserving the Fund’s capital by limiting annual withdrawal to one-half of its expected real return and confining its use to only education, healthcare and climate change mitigation and adaptation purposes; and National Trust Fund 25 (c) establishing the Board of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) (“the Board”) with clear duties and powers and strengthening its functions regarding investments of the Fund. Part I 2. Part I of the proposed Act deals with preliminary matters. 3. Clause 1 contains the short title of the proposed Act and seeks to empower the Minister to appoint a date for the commencement of the proposed Act. 4. Clause 2 contains the definitions of certain words and expressions used in the proposed Act. Part II 5. Part II of the proposed Act deals with the National Trust Fund and its governance and contains twenty-one provisions divided into two Divisions. Division 1 6. Division 1 of Part II deals with the provisions relating to the National Trust Fund. 7. Clause 3 seeks to provide for the reestablishment of the Fund. Moneys standing in or due to be paid to the National Trust Fund under the repealed Act shall be transferred to the Fund. As at 31 December 2024, the National Trust Fund’s net assets at the group level amounted to RM22.43 billion. 8. Clause 4 seeks to provide for the contributions to the Fund. Subclause 4(1) places the contributions on a broad and mandatory statutory footing, in place of the voluntary basis under the repealed Act. Since the establishment of the National Trust Fund in 1988, Petroliam Nasional Berhad (PETRONAS) has been its sole contributor, with the contribution amount varying from year to year at the discretion of the Board of PETRONAS. This clause requires contributions by the Federal Government of, firstly a minimum of 0.1% of its projected annual revenue, secondly a minimum of 2% of the dividend received from PETRONAS, and thirdly a minimum of 2% from the export duty received by the Federal Government on depleting resources. Under clause 2, “depleting resources” is defined as crude oil, mineral ores, iron ore or any other natural resources which may be susceptible to depletion. For clarification, the contribution amount linked to export duty is computed only on the portion forming part of the revenue of the Federal Government and does not affect any portion of the duty assigned to a State Government under Article 110 of the Federal Constitution. 9. Clause 5 seeks to provide for other contributions which may be voluntarily paid into the Fund, namely contributions by any State Government which derives royalty from petroleum or other depleting resources and income from investments of the Fund. This clause was provided for in the repealed Act and is adopted into the proposed Act. 10. Clause 6 seeks to provide for expenditure to be charged on the Fund. 11. Clause 7 seeks to empower the Minister to require the Board to furnish returns, reports, accounts and other information in respect of the Fund. Division 2 12. Division 2 of Part II deals with the provisions relating to the National Trust Fund (Incorporated). 13. Clause 8 seeks to provide for the incorporation of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to hold property and to sue and be sued in its own name. This confers legal personality to the National Trust Fund (Incorporated). 14. Clause 9 seeks to provide for the functions and powers of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated), that is to administer, manage and invest the Fund. 15. Clause 10 seeks to provide for the common seal of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) and for its authentication. 16. Clause 11 seeks to provide for the appointment of the Board of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) (“the Board”), which shall consist of a Chairperson, a Deputy Chairperson who is an officer of the Ministry of Finance, an officer from the Prime Minister’s Department, and between two to four persons with the knowledge, experience and expertise in business, investment, banking or finance. All members are to be appointed by the Minister. 17. Clause 12 seeks to provide for the duties and powers of the Board. The Board shall primarily be responsible for the administration and management of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) and investment of the Fund. Subclauses 12(2) and 12(3) seek to allow the Board to delegate any of its powers to any person as it deems necessary, subject to the approval of the Minister. However, such delegation does not preclude the Board from exercising the powers so delegated. Subclause 12(5) seeks to empower the Board to establish committees to assist in the performance of its duties and the exercise of its powers. 18. Clause 13 seeks to provide for the remuneration of members of the Board. National Trust Fund 27 19. bills.title: Statistics Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Tuan Haji Akmal Nasrullah bin Mohd Nasir, Menteri Ekonomi
bills.explanation: The Bill (“the proposed Act”) seeks to provide for the functions of the Department of Statistics Malaysia, establishment of the National Statistics Council, matters relating to data and statistics and other related matters. Part I 2. Part I of the proposed Act deals with the preliminary matters. 3. Clause 1 contains the short title of the proposed Act and seeks to empower the Minister to appoint a date for the commencement of the proposed Act. 4. Clause 2 seeks to provide that the proposed Act binds the Federal Government and State Government. 5. Clause 3 contains the definition of certain words and expressions used in the proposed Act. Part II 6. Part II of the proposed Act deals with the provisions relating to the Department of Statistics Malaysia. 7. Clause 4 seeks to provide for the appointment of the Chief Statistician, Deputy Chief Statistician and such other officer of the Department of Statistics Malaysia. 8. Clause 5 seeks to provide for the functions of the Department of Statistics Malaysia. 9. Clause 6 seeks to enable the Chief Statistician to delegate his powers to any Deputy Chief Statistician or officer of the Department of Statistics Malaysia. Part III 10. Part III of the proposed Act deals with the provisions relating to the National Statistics Council (“Council”). 11. Clause 7 seeks to provide for the establishment and the membership of the Council. 12. Clause 8 seeks to allow the Council to invite any person to attend any meeting of the Council. 13. Clause 9 seeks to provide for the functions of the Council. 14. Clause 10 seeks to provide for matters relating to meetings of the Council. Statistics 15 15. Clause 11 seeks to empower the Council to establish any committee and to provide for the matters relating to it. Part IV 16. Part IV of the proposed Act deals with the provisions relating to data collection, publication and communication. 17. Clause 12 seeks to provide that the Chief Statistician may, in the form and manner and within the period as specified in the notice or such extended period as the Chief Statistician may grant, direct any person to furnish such data within the person’s knowledge or which the person is reasonably able to obtain. 18. Clause 13 seeks to provide that the Chief Statistician may request any data from any Government entity by notice in writing directing the head of Government entity to furnish the data. 19. Clause 14 seeks to provide for the requirements for the publication and communication of data or statistics. This clause also provides that the request for data or statistics may be made in the form and manner determined by the Chief Statistician and the prescribed fee shall be paid. Part V 20. Clause 16 seeks to provide for the protection of the Minister, any member of the Council, the Chief Statistician, any Deputy Chief Statistician or officer of the Department of Statistics Malaysia from suit and legal proceedings in respect of any act, neglect or default done or omitted by him in carrying out his duties under the proposed Act. 23. Clause 17 deals with the liability of a director, compliance officer, partner, manager, secretary or other similar officer in respect of an offence committed by a company, limited liability partnership, firm, society or other body of persons under the proposed Act. 24. Clause 18 seeks to empower the Minister to make regulations under the proposed Act. 25. Clause 19 seeks to empower the Chief Statistician to issue any directive, circular or guidelines for the purpose of carrying into effect the provisions of the proposed Act. 26. Part VI of the proposed Act deals with the repeal provision. 28. Clause 21 seeks to provide for the repeal of the Statistics Act 1965 [Act 415]. 29. Clause 22 deals with saving provision.

bills.title: Freedom of Information Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Dato' Sri Azalina binti Othman Said, Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Undang-Undang dan Reformasi Institusi)
bills.explanation: This Bill (“the proposed Act”) is enacted pursuant to items 4(f) and 6 of the Federal List with the Ninth Schedule of the Federal Constitution, namely “ official secrets” and “the machinery of government including federal public authorities”. The proposed Act seeks to establish a procedural mechanism to regulate requests by any person for access to information contained in any official document within the control of the public authorities. The proposed Act provides that any person, who is a citizen of Malaysia aged eighteen and above, may request for access to information in accordance with its provisions. The proposed Act is purely procedural in nature and is intended solely to regulate the process for requesting, considering and determining applications for access to information. The proposed Act is without prejudice to the operation of any written law governing the confidentiality or non-disclosure of information. Accordingly, information classified as an official secret under the Official Secrets Act 1972 [Act 88], and any official document, secret, confidential information or other information the disclosure of which is prohibited, restricted or otherwise protected under any written law, is excluded from the application of the proposed Act. In other words, the proposed Act preserves the primacy of existing secrecy statutes while making clear that the proposed legislation creates only a procedural mechanism for requesting access to information, not an overriding substantive right of disclosure. The proposed Act provides a two-tier internal review mechanism whereby a person may seek a review of a decision made by an appointed officer of the public authority in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the proposed Act. The jurisdiction and powers of the head of public authority under the internal review process are subject to the same limitations, exemptions and exclusions applicable to requests for access to information under the proposed Act and no head of public authority may require or authorise the disclosure of information excluded from the operation of the proposed Act. The proposed Act also provides for a further external review by the Ombudsman. Although the Ombudsman is established as a body corporate under the Ombudsman Act 20… [Act …], for the purposes of the proposed Act, it performs administrative functions (i.e. being a body under the purview of the Executive) and exercises only such jurisdiction and powers as are expressly conferred by the proposed Act. The Ombudsman has no jurisdiction to review, require the disclosure of, or make any determination in respect of information that is excluded from the operation of the proposed Act or the disclosure of which is prohibited, restricted or otherwise protected under the Official Secrets Act 1972 or any other written law. In addition, an aggrieved person may apply for judicial review against the decision of the Ombudsman or the public authority. Besides that, nothing in the proposed Act shall be construed as creating, conferring or recognising a substantive right to information as a fundamental liberty under the Federal Constitution nor shall it be construed as recognising or conferring any right relating to the freedom of the press or the media. Therefore, the proposed Act provides for the procedure for making requests for access to information, the duties of public authorities in dealing with such requests, the categories of information excluded from disclosure, the two- tier internal review mechanism, the external review by the Ombudsman, and to provide for related matters. Part I 2. Part I of the proposed Act contains preliminary matters. 3. Clause 1 contains the short title of the proposed Act and provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 4. Clause 2 seeks to provide for the application of the proposed Act. Subclause 2(1) seeks to provide that the proposed Act shall apply to the Federal Government. Subclause 2(2) seeks to provide that the proposed Act provides for the procedure to request for access to information subject to exempted information under this proposed Act. Subclause 2(3) seeks to provide that the proposed Act shall be read together with the provisions of other written laws that allow access to official documents, and the provisions of the proposed Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of the relevant written laws. Freedom of Information 19 5. Clause 3 contains the definitions of certain words and expressions used in the proposed Act, among others, the definition of “information” and “public authority”. In the proposed Act, the definition of “information” shall be construed to be within the ambit of clause 9 only which excludes, among others, all information classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act 1972, and any official document, secret, confidential information or other information the disclosure of which is prohibited, restricted or otherwise protected under any written law. On the other hand, the definition of “public authority” is intended to identify the Federal entities to which the proposed Act applies. Paragraph (a) includes the Federal Government, encompassing the Ministries, departments and offices forming part of the Federal administration. Paragraph (b) includes the Parliamentary Service established under the Parliamentary Service Act 2025 [Act 869]. Although the Parliamentary Service operates independently of the Executive, it performs public functions and is therefore brought within the scope of the proposed Act. Paragraph (c) includes statutory bodies of the Federal Government established under an Act of Parliament. This ensures that Federal statutory authorities created by written law and exercising statutory powers or performing public functions are subject to the proposed Act. Paragraph (d) includes the local authorities of the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya. As local government within the Federal
